title: Central Overload Build-Up
definition: A build-up strategy that creates numerical superiority in the central zone to force opponents to drop deeper, thereby opening space on the flanks or for the striker.
content: This tactical concept involves establishing a 4v2 or 4v3 numerical advantage in the central midfield area during the build-up phase. By concentrating players in the middle, the team forces the opposition to react by dropping their forwards (e.g., the 9 and 10) to maintain a 4v4 or 5v5 balance. This reaction creates two key opportunities: first, it leaves the wide areas or the space behind the defensive line open for wingers or attacking midfielders to exploit; second, it allows the team to control possession and switch play to the opposite side where players are now free of pressure. If the opponent fails to drop and maintains a high line, the central overloads can directly penetrate or switch play. A critical component is the goalkeeper's role; if the opponent presses aggressively, the goalkeeper drops to become an extra passing option, allowing the team to reset the build-up and maintain the numerical advantage. This approach is particularly effective against teams playing with a single pivot or a 4-2-3-1 structure, where the central midfield is vulnerable to overloading.
